External / portable drive · Corrupted / RAW / asks to format

Fix a Corrupted or Unreadable External Hard Drive

Corruption often follows pulling the cable without ejecting, a power cut or failing parts. It means the drive's records of where files are got damaged, and the files are often still there. Do not run repair tools on the original first, because they can change your data.

3/5 · Take care
Success odds: Medium

The drive may be weak, and repair tools such as CHKDSK on the original can change data before you have a copy.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not run CHKDSK, fsck or Disk Utility's First Aid on the original before copying your data.
  • Do not click Format when the computer says the drive needs formatting.
  • Do not install recovery software onto the affected drive or save files back to it.

Your steps

0 of 6 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Windows: click the USB icon in the taskbar, then Eject. Mac: click the eject button next to the drive in Finder.
    2. If it clicks or grinds, unplug it and read our clicking guide instead.
  2. Show me how
    1. Windows: install and open CrystalDiskInfo and read the Health Status. Linux live USB: in the Terminal (Ctrl+Alt+T) type sudo apt install smartmontools, then sudo smartctl -a /dev/sdX (some USB cases need -d sat after smartctl). Mac: see the health check guide.
    2. Some USB cases hide SMART, so a missing report does not mean the drive is fine.

    Guide: How to check if a drive is healthy (SMART)

  3. Show me how
    1. Plug directly into the computer, not through a hub, with a different cable.
    2. Keep the drive in its case, because many WD drives encrypt data through the case's board.
  4. Show me how
    1. Check the damaged drive's size in File Explorer or Disk Utility.
    2. Use a different drive with at least that much free space.
  5. Show me how
    1. Boot a Linux live USB, press Ctrl+Alt+T to open a terminal, install ddrescue with sudo apt install gddrescue, then run lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL to identify both drives. Open the destination drive in the Files app, but not the damaged one.
    2. Run sudo ddrescue -n /dev/sdX /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.img /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.map, where sdX is the damaged drive and DEST is your destination drive's name (Linux Mint: /media/mint/DEST). Always type the failing drive first and the empty destination second. If you swap them, the copy erases your data.
    3. Keep the map file so you can stop and resume. HDDSuperClone is an alternative on Linux.

    Guide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a driveGuide: How to make a Linux live USB (step by step)

  6. Show me how
    1. Run sudo testdisk /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.img to rebuild partitions or list files, and copy them to another drive.
    2. If folders are too damaged, run sudo photorec /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.img. Never work on the original.

    Guide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Tools you'll use

GNU ddrescue

Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

  • Linux · macOS
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

ddrescueview

Free graphical viewer that shows which parts of a ddrescue image are good, bad or still unread.

  • Windows · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

HDDSuperClone

Linux tool for cloning a failing drive sector by sector, with options that skip and retry bad areas.

  • Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

CrystalDiskInfo

Free Windows app that shows a drive's S.M.A.R.T. health status, temperature and other key attributes.

  • Windows
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

PhotoRec

Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

Questions people ask

Should I run CHKDSK first?

No. It can rewrite damaged data. Image the drive first and repair or recover from the copy.

Why does it say the drive is RAW?

The computer cannot read the drive's file system, which is its way of organising files, often because of an unsafe unplug or damage. TestDisk can often restore it.

Why can't I see SMART data?

Many USB cases do not pass it through. That is common and does not mean the drive is healthy.
